fusillade

FYOO-suh-lahd · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Fusillade is a rapid series of shots fired, especially all at once or in quick succession.

A fusillade of bottle rockets erupted over the lake at exactly midnight.

Example

The general ordered a fusillade to cover the retreating troops as they crossed the bridge.

This wasn't a single shot -- it was a rapid burst of many shots fired together, which is exactly a fusillade.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

barrage: A barrage is a heavy, concentrated outpouring that keeps coming -- artillery pounding a position for hours, or a barrage of questions that never lets up. A fusillade is quicker and lighter: a rapid burst of many shots or remarks delivered in seconds, and then it is over.

volley: A volley is one coordinated discharge -- many shots released together at the same instant, usually on command, and then it is done. A fusillade keeps going: shot after shot in rapid succession, a burst with real duration rather than a single organized instant.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

ceasefire: a temporary stop to fighting

Where it sits · how heavy and sustained the gunfire — shot → fusillade → bombardment

shot vs. fusillade: A single shot is one report; a fusillade is many shots fired rapidly, one after another or all at once.

bombardment vs. fusillade: A fusillade is a rapid burst of small-arms fire; a bombardment is a sustained, heavier assault, often with artillery.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Fusillade comes from French fusiller ('to shoot'), itself from fusil ('a flintlock gun'), plus -ade, a suffix marking an action or its result.

Use the root in a new word: fuel

Use the root in a new word: fuel: French fusil, the flintlock gun, goes back to Latin focus, 'hearth, fire' -- and fuel descends from that very same focus. A gun and the firewood it might spark turn out to share one fire root.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Fusillade can describe literal gunfire or, in a non-literal sense, any rapid, overwhelming burst -- a fusillade of questions, a fusillade of complaints.
